suggestions.quote: the glowing chip over a head
suggestions.fix: style.md lists 'neon counters over heads' as a ConChaser signature not to copy. Build the chip as a cream paper tag with a split-flap number on a short stalk, with a soft crimson rim glow only on yours. This also keeps the on-screen text to the allowed forms (tag or counter).

suggestions.quote: the hall becomes one lit chair among two thousand five hundred
suggestions.fix: This is the heaviest build, so make it one instanced grid of identical paper chairs (a single shape repeated, one chair lit) with a slow camera pull-back. Use the same instanced head-and-chip grid for the 400-student hall in line 33 so both scenes come from one asset.

suggestions.quote: The city lit up, built only from people we know
suggestions.fix: Keep the city to 3 or 4 drifting depth layers of flat blocks, with a lit window or chip for each of the four known people. The teacher, topper, chaiwala and cousin come from line 35 and are not new sets. Do not add a new street set.

suggestions.quote: First, the lane at home: your younger cousin bowls to you
suggestions.fix: Five sets are named: hall, lane, chai stall, topper's keyboard, city. Mark in the G2 script which are new and which reuse the pause-time kit. Reuse the kid (cap) rig for the cousin, and make the bat a single prop that appears in the lane, rolls away at line 36, is hidden at line 37 and returns at line 38.

suggestions.quote: his chip drains to zero the moment he nods, his hand leaves the bat, and it rolls out of frame
suggestions.fix: Stage the peak at 8 to 10 s with a change every 2 to 4 s: the chip's split-flap counts down, the colour drains from his head, a slow-motion ghost follows the hand, and the bat rolls. Keep text off his face and put the chip above the cap.

suggestions.quote: the hall becomes one lit chair among two thousand five hundred, then back to your face
suggestions.fix: Set the colour rule now. Everyone in the hall wears pastel heads and ink bodies, and only you and the cousin keep full colour. The crimson stranger stays hidden in a back row of the hall for the second-watch plant.

suggestions.quote: Row three. You don't look up. Out in the lane: thwack.
suggestions.fix: Keep the right third empty for the last 15 s. Frame you at left of centre, and give the thwack as a sound over a held, slightly drifting image of the empty lane at the screen's left, with no on-screen text.

suggestions.quote: First seven seconds, the thumbnail's picture
suggestions.fix: The thumbnail has you large at left looking at the chip beside your head. Open on that exact framing, then pull out to row three, so the click is confirmed and the shot is stageable side-on.

cues.yaml is not in my inputs, so I cannot check the G2 sound checks (one-word intent per beat, music changes at or after a reveal). At G2, supply cues.yaml and keep the music change at the chip reveal (line 33) and at the bat's roll (line 36), not before them.
